comments.body: Updated: #2802 has been superseded by #2839 (rebased on current main).
How about spdlog which already include fmt?

@julianoes fmtlib is just a formatting library, spdlog is a logger with sinks, levels etc. It uses fmtlib or std::format under the hood. Also, if you are planning to use c++20 than std::format is supported from gcc13, but not sure if there are issues for other platforms like android/ios.

> [@julianoes](https://github.com/julianoes) fmtlib is just a formatting library, spdlog is a logger with sinks, levels etc. It uses fmtlib or std::format under the hood. Also, if you are planning to use c++20 than std::format is supported from gcc13, but not sure if there are issues for other platforms like android/ios. IMHO `std::format` performance is much worse across the board. Actually I don't know If this white elephant is used anywhere in production. Benchmark code link - https://godbolt.org/z/WY7vP9b8n . P.S `std::format` is supported from `GCC 13` and `NDK r27+ (Clang/libc++)`, though iOS/Apple Clang may still have gaps. `fmtlib` remains the portable fallback.

> > [@julianoes](https://github.com/julianoes) fmtlib is just a formatting library, spdlog is a logger with sinks, levels etc. It uses fmtlib or std::format under the hood. Also, if you are planning to use c++20 than std::format is supported from gcc13, but not sure if there are issues for other platforms like android/ios. > > IMHO `std::format` performance is much worse across the board. Actually I don't know If this white elephant is used anywhere in production. Benchmark code link - https://godbolt.org/z/WY7vP9b8n . > > > P.S `std::format` is supported from `GCC 13` and `NDK r27+ (Clang/libc++)`, though iOS/Apple Clang may still have gaps. `fmtlib` remains the portable fallback. You forgot the main thing for benchmarks: build with full optimizations (`compiled with -O2` is just a cout in your link). The ratios dropped down to average around 0.3x, std::format is a winner. Me personally, I am not for or against fmt/std formatting, std is based on fmt at the end. For such low difference in performance I would rather not use external libs if possible for sake of simplicity. However, as mavsdk need to support some old compilers and systems fmtlib is a choice. The main idea is to propose spdlog which will simplify logging.

You guys are a bit late to the party. See more rational in https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2815#issue-4161803549.

Initially, I wanted to just use C++20 std::format but quickly discovered that support for the platforms we currently support was patchy. (We build with GCC 9 for some older platforms.)

Claude Code quickly added a "fallback" to go back to std::ostream based printing and manual parsing for `{}` for older platforms but I did not want to have two implementations to track where the slower one was likely used on older (and likely) slower platforms. Therefore, I decided to end the `std::format` experiment and use `fmt` instead.

@jazzvaz you mention spdlog? What benefit would that give us?

I see. I wonder if this would solve the issue with platforms like Android where you can't (or at least not easily) set the env variable in the first place. Presumably, spdlog would help with that. I'm a bit reluctant to change this myself but I would consider a pull request.

issue.title: Expose full HOME_POSITION fields in subscribe_home

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
## Summary
- Add new `HomePosition` struct with all fields from MAVLink HOME_POSITION message (#242)
- `subscribe_home` now returns `HomePosition` instead of `Position` (breaking API change)
- New fields: local NED (x/y/z), surface quaternion, approach vector, timestamp
- Add system test verifying all fields propagate correctly end-to-end

## Motivation
Fixes #2310 — `subscribe_home` only returns global GPS position but HOME_POSITION also carries local NED position, attitude quaternion, approach vector, and timestamp that were being silently discarded.

## Changes
- **Proto**: Add `HomePosition` message, change `HomeResponse` to use it
- **Header**: Add `HomePosition` struct, update `HomeCallback`/`HomeHandle` types
- **Impl**: Populate all HOME_POSITION fields in `process_home_position()`
- **gRPC**: Add `translateToRpcHomePosition`/`translateFromRpcHomePosition`
- **Test**: System test `HomePositionFullFields` validates all fields

## Breaking Change
`subscribe_home` callback type changes from `std::function<void(Position)>` to `std::function<void(HomePosition)>`. `HomePosition` is a superset of `Position` — the same lat/lon/alt fields are present at the same offsets.

## Companion PR
Proto changes: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/pull/399

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests pass (289/289)
- [x] System test `HomePositionFullFields` passes — validates GPS, local NED, quaternion, approach vector, and timestamp
- [x] Build clean

issue.title: test: rename system tests from SystemTest suite to per-plugin suites

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
Part of v4 plan: #2830.

Splits the monolithic `SystemTest` suite into 13 per-plugin/area suites so tests appear as e.g. `Ftp.UploadFile` instead of `SystemTest.FtpUploadFile`.

New suites: `Action`, `Camera`, `ComponentMetadata`, `Connections`, `Ftp`, `Geofence`, `Intercept`, `MavlinkDirect`, `MavlinkSeq`, `Mission`, `Param`, `RawBytes`, `Telemetry`.

All 83 tests renamed, purely mechanical change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issue.title: refactor: rename all public C++ headers from .h to .hpp

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
Part of v4 plan: #2830.

Renames all 55 public headers under `include/mavsdk/` and `include/plugins/*/` from `.h` to `.hpp` to follow the C++ convention of using `.hpp` for C++-only headers.

Updated across 333 files:
- Internal mavsdk core and plugin sources
- mavsdk_server gRPC service implementations
- Examples
- Jinja2 code generation templates
- `CMakeLists.txt` `install(FILES ...)` rules

**Breaking change for v4**: downstream code including `<mavsdk/mavsdk.h>`, `<mavsdk/plugins/action/action.h>`, etc. must update to `.hpp`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
